scenario: Research seed dispatch, with independently sealed jars sharing one accession and late laboratory evidence.

defects.title: Accession clearance authorizes an untested sibling jar

contract_sources.quote: A negative result for another jar does not authorize this jar.

An accession row holds species, collection location and harvest date.
A jar row holds jar_id, accession_id, generation, shelf and lifecycle.

implementation_sources.quote:
The gateway maintains accession_clearance keyed by accession_id.
A NEGATIVE result sets that accession clearance to RELEASED.

After reserving the jar, look up its current accession_id in local clearance.
A RELEASED row allows the ticket transaction to commit.

counterexample: NB-71 has J-A generation 1 and J-B generation 1, both initially held.
Receive NEGATIVE for S-A sampled from J-A generation 1; deliver its clearance snapshot.
Reserve J-B and create a ticket using NB-71 RELEASED. No matching evidence for J-B exists.
defects.cause: The aggregate used for scientific navigation has been made the owner of physical eligibility; a sample loses its jar scope at the gateway boundary.
defects.repair_principle: Preserve physical jar and sampled generation in eligibility evidence, and require the selected jar to match. Jar-only isolation fixes sibling authorization but does not fix D2.

defects.title: A new seal generation can be dispatched using stale or late old-generation clearance

contract_sources.quote: A negative result for an older seal generation does not authorize the current one.

The opening transaction increments generation and records the operator.
It writes a JarResealed event with the new generation in the same commit.

implementation_sources.quote:
Reset and receipt updates are processed in local arrival order.
The row lock serializes simultaneous handlers for the same accession.
There is no comparison of a result's sampled generation with current generation.

The local row is the authority used for biological eligibility.
No synchronous gateway call is made during a pick.

The gateway outbox can be delayed independently of registry work.
A valid registry lease does not wait for gateway queue delivery.

counterexample: Receive and deliver S-A NEGATIVE for J-A generation 1.
Reseal J-A to generation 2, committing the registry event. Delay the gateway reset or its delivery.
A fresh lease freezes generation 2, but the old local RELEASED row permits a generation 2 ticket.
additional_counterexample: Reseal J-A to generation 2; process and deliver its reset so it is HELD.
Receive the delayed S-A generation 1 negative; ordinary receipt processing sets RELEASED at a newer revision.
Deliver it; generation 2 can now receive a ticket even after all queues drain.
defects.cause: Registry owns current physical generation, but dispatch authorization belongs to an asynchronously updated accession projection with no generation fence. Revisions order gateway writes, not sampled biological state.
defects.repair_principle: Require evidence for the current jar generation while holding the registry work lease. Coordinate matching prevents stale results from gaining scope; the lease prevents a generation change between lookup and draw. Merely processing event resets faster or adding a global row lock is insufficient.
defects.witness: Second and third unauthorized traces in hidden/witness.py

sources.quote: The gateway maintains sample_clearance keyed by (jar_id, sampled_generation).
No lookup falls back from an unknown generation to an older one.

Hold the work lease across primary registry read, evidence lookup and ticket commit.
Commit only when matching negative evidence exists for the frozen coordinates.

The configured pilot has no final-result revocation or evidence expiry.
Thus a received matching negative stays valid during that reserved interval.
The lease excludes resealing between evidence lookup and the authorized draw.
The pilot permits at most one registered assay sample per jar generation.

correct_packet_guarantee.argument: Negative evidence is immutable and scoped to exact coordinates. Dispatch freezes current coordinates with the shared physical-work lease and reads matching evidence synchronously. Delayed receipt cannot change its scope; delayed inventory events cannot create evidence. No revocation/expiry exists in this bounded pilot, so no distributed transaction with Gateway is needed during the lease.

false_alarms: An accession grouping in the dashboard is harmless in q because it is not an authorization input.
At-least-once result delivery is handled by immutable result_id and atomic receipt/projection/outbox writes.
A delayed old-generation result is safe in q; it remains historical evidence for its sampled coordinates.
No global queue ordering is required in q, and a distributed transaction spanning Registry and Gateway is not required under immutable evidence plus the shared lease.
The physical scan-before-opening assumption is explicit, not an undocumented technical guarantee. Scanner failures are routed to a supervisor.
Permit checks and seed quantity accounting are explicitly separate workflows; missing details do not prove a defect in this eligibility decision.
unknown_policies: Destination-specific certificates for future overseas recipients.
model_limits: Finite model covers one immutable negative sample, two physical jars and a single reseal.
No claim to prove all production behavior; scenario is synthetic.
Lease atomicity, scan-before-opening and scientific assay validity are supplied assumptions in the review documents.
Unspecified policies are not filled in by the witness.
